title: Telemetry-driven Eval Prioritization and Hotspot Triage
author: Eleanor Ruiz
content:
Summary
This document describes a telemetry-first system for prioritizing offline and online evaluation jobs and a structured hotspot triage playbook for high-impact model behavior regressions. It targets the evaluator orchestration layer and SRE/Applied-ML engineers who run and act on model quality telemetry for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Motivation
- The eval backlog grows faster than evaluation capacity. Manual triage leads to missed regressions and wasted compute on low-impact slices.
- Telemetry (production errors, user rejections, SLA anomalies) is an early indicator of quality regressions but needs automated translation into eval work.
- We need a deterministic, auditable prioritization pipeline that: (1) converts telemetry to eval tasks, (2) assigns cost-aware priority, and (3) feeds actionable triage runbooks to on-call and ML engineers.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Surface the top-K evaluation tasks that reduce user-impact most per compute dollar.
  - Ensure high-recall capture of hotspots without overwhelming evaluators.
  - Provide an operator-facing triage checklist with concrete rollback/fallback actions.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a model promotion gate (that remains the model-onboarding pipeline).
  - It does not supersede security or privacy reviews for customer data.

Principles
1) Signal-first: prioritize signals with clear business impact (error rates, retention drops, user-text flags).
2) Cost-awareness: include token/throughput cost estimates in prioritization.
3) Explainability: each prioritized eval job must include the telemetry-derived rationale and suggested slices.
4) Fast feedback: support micro-canaries and quick smoke evals (<30m) before full-scale runs.

Telemetry signals (inputs)
- Production traces: streaming error labels (500-series), latency p99/p50 spikes, timeouts.
- User feedback: explicit thumbs-down, A/B experiment metrics (CTR/retention deltas).
- Quality analytics: semantic drift detectors, embedding-distance anomalies, stability score drops.
- Routing & capacity: fallback events (requests routed to cheaper model variants).

Signal enrichment steps
1) Attach context: request metadata (model version, route, top-k prompts), tenant_id, and sequence length buckets.
2) Cluster related events: temporal proximity (5–15m windows), similar prompt fingerprints (edit distance or embedding cosine > 0.92).
3) Score impact: compute an impact score (0–100) combining user count, error severity, and retention delta.

Priority scoring algorithm (overview)
- Inputs: impact_score, estimated_eval_cost (core-hours or token-cost), urgency_multiplier (customer SLA tier), seasonality_factor.
- Priority = (impact_score * urgency_multiplier * seasonality_factor) / (1 + log(1 + estimated_eval_cost))
- Normalization: scale to 0–100 and bucket into: critical (>80), high (60–80), medium (30–60), low (<30).

Eval task generation
1) Auto-slice suggestion: generate 3–7 candidate slices using clustering (intent, length, locale, prompt-token prefix).
2) Quick smoke: spawn a 30m micro-eval on a 500–2k sample (approx 5–20k tokens) to confirm signal.
3) Full evaluation: if smoke fails, schedule full eval with stratified sampling across traffic segments.

Hotspot triage playbook (operator steps)
1) Acknowledge: Owner (on-call ML or SRE) acknowledges the prioritized task in the evaluation dashboard within 30 minutes for critical tasks.
2) Run smoke eval: launch the micro-sample smoke eval. If pass -> mark as false-positive and document reasoning.
3) If smoke fails: run a targeted full eval job and fetch comparison baselines (previous model version and quantized variant).
4) Determine root cause categories (choose one primary):
   - Model drift / distribution shift
   - Quantization-induced degradation
   - Serving KV-cache/latency artifact
   - Prompt-processing bug (pre/post-processing mismatch)
   - Data corruption / formatting errors
5) For each root cause, follow the remediation checklist below.

Remediation checklists (short)
- Model drift:
  - Compare top-k token distributions and embedding centroids versus baseline.
  - Re-run eval with increased context/contextual shots.
  - If confirmed, create model-promotion hold ticket; notify product and release manager.
- Quantization-induced degradation:
  - Re-run on full-precision replica and mixed-precision replicas.
  - If degradation isolated to q4/q8 profile, revert to higher-fidelity profile for affected routes and open quant-team ticket.
- KV-cache / latency artifact:
  - Check per-token latency, cache hit rates, and request-shard mapping.
  - Warm caches for affected routes and schedule a controlled roll-forward.
- Prompt-processing bug:
  - Replay raw request through offline preprocessing; compare outputs.
  - Patch preprocessor and deploy a canary.
- Data corruption:
  - Validate ingestion pipelines and normalization; block bad batches and backfill missing fields.

Escalation and rollback policy
- Critical priority: if a full eval shows regression (>5% degradations on primary metric for top-tier customers), perform an emergency rollback to the last certified model and notify Incident Response.
- High priority: consider partial route-level fallback to a previous variant; schedule a postmortem if rollback is performed.

Operational configurations (table)
| Config name | Default | Range | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke_eval_sample_size | 1000 | 500–5000 | sample count for micro-evaluations |
| smoke_eval_duration | 30m | 5m–120m | duration limit before automatic cancel |
| eval_cost_threshold_usd | 200 | 50–2000 | above threshold requires manager approval |
| critical_priority_threshold | 80 | 70–100 | score threshold for critical routing |
| max_parallel_smoke_jobs | 20 | 1–100 | global concurrency cap |

Automation and tooling hooks
- Orchestration: eval-orch service (internal) integrates with telemetry bus and can enqueue tasks into the evaluator fleet.
- Dashboard: "Eval Hotspots" view shows live prioritized queue, rationale, sample prompts, and quick-run buttons.
- CLI examples:
  - Queue a micro-smoke: evalctl run --slice-id S12345 --mode smoke --sample 1000
  - Fetch rationale: evalctl show --task T98765 --rationale

Metrics and SLOs for the pipeline
- Time to acknowledge (critical): 30 minutes (target 90th percentile).
- Time to smoke result: 45 minutes from enqueue (including scheduling).
- False positive rate for prioritized tasks: <20% (measured quarterly).
- Coverage: >95% of telemetry events with impact_score >= 40 must surface a prioritized eval job or a documented suppression rule.

Ownership and contact list
- Primary owner: Applied ML - Eval Orchestration (team lead: Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime Reliability (team lead: Miguel Santos)
- Pager rotations and on-call: see /confluence/eng-oncall/oncall-rotations for links.

Audit and compliance notes
- All eval jobs spawned from customer traffic must log the minimal request fingerprint and must not store PII in evaluation payloads. The eval-orch enforces scrubbing policies described in the privacy contract.

Appendix: example prioritized payload (human-readable)
- Alert ID: ALERT-2026-1421
- Rationale: p99 latency spike for route /chat/stream; 12k impacted users, 0.7% retention drop over 1h window
- Suggested slices: long-context > 1024 tokens, locale: en-US, intent: summarization
- Estimated eval cost: $340 (full), $28 (smoke)
- Priority score: 87 (critical)

- See drift detection and embedding stability guidelines for signal extraction patterns.
